description: Verify that an ARP conflict on the offered address triggers a DHCPDECLINE (msg_type=4, ciaddr=0, Option 50 = declined yiaddr, Option 54 = server_id) (RFC 2131 §4.4.1 / §4.4.4 MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
When the post-BOUND ARP Probe collides with a real holder, the offered address is unusable. The client must tell the server with a DHCPDECLINE — pointing at the address (Option 50) and the server that gave it (Option 54) — so the server can mark the address bad.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. DORA: DISCOVER → OFFER → REQUEST → ACK → BOUND.
2. DUT → wire: ARP Probe targeting yiaddr.
3. Tester → DUT: ARP Reply claiming yiaddr (the conflict).
4. DUT → wire: DHCPDECLINE
   • msg_type = 4
   • ciaddr = 0
   • Option 50 = declined yiaddr
   • Option 54 = server_id   ← key check

[Pass condition]
DHCPDECLINE with the expected fields lands within the deadline.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_discover / Fail_no_request / Fail_no_arp_probe — DORA / Probe missing
• Fail_no_decline — DUT did not emit DHCPDECLINE after the ARP conflict

verdicts.Pass: DUT emitted DHCPDECLINE after ARP conflict — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_discover: No DUT DHCPDISCOVER within the listen window
verdicts.Fail_no_arp_probe: No DUT ARP Probe after BOUND
verdicts.Fail_no_decline: No DUT DHCPDECLINE after ARP conflict
